stem: Meera starts facing north. She turns 90 degrees clockwise, then walks 8 m. She then turns 90 degrees anticlockwise and walks 6 m. She finally turns 180 degrees. In which direction is she now facing?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student treats the final 180 degrees turn as a 90 degrees left turn from North, arriving at West instead of South.
Student skips the final 180 degrees turn and reports the direction after the first clockwise turn, giving East.
Student skips the final 180 degrees turn entirely, reporting North after the second segment.
Start N, CW 90 degrees -> E, walk 8 m. ACW 90 degrees from E -> N, walk 6 m. 180 degrees from N -> S. Final direction: South.

explanation: Start facing North. Turn CW 90 degrees: now facing East. Walk 8 m. Turn ACW 90 degrees from East: now facing North. Walk 6 m. Turn 180 degrees from North: now facing South.

explanation_sections.punchline: After two turns that cancel each other out, Meera is again facing North. A final 180-degree turn points her South.
explanation_sections.approach: For direction problems, track only the facing direction at each step. Write a short chain: N, CW 90 = E, ACW 90 from E = N, 180 from N = S. Distance walked does not change the facing direction. Apply turns in order and do not skip any.
explanation_sections.lesson: A clockwise 90-degree turn followed by an anticlockwise 90-degree turn returns you to the original direction. A 180-degree turn always points you in the exact opposite direction.
explanation_sections.timing: About 90 seconds. Each turn takes under 10 seconds to resolve. The entire chain has three turns. Read every turn before writing down the final answer to avoid missing the last step.
